approachQuestion.prompt:
Convex safety zone

A strictly convex polygon is supplied as n distinct vertices in cyclic boundary order, either clockwise or counterclockwise. Given integer point P, return whether it lies inside the polygon or on its boundary.

Example 1: polygon=[(0,0),(4,0),(4,3),(0,3)],P=(2,1) -> true.
Example 2: the same polygon,P=(4,1) -> true.
Example 3: the same polygon,P=(5,1) -> false.
Example 4: polygon=[(0,0),(4,0),(0,4)],P=(3,3) -> false.

Constraints and assumptions: 3 <= n <= 200000; all coordinates, including P, are integers in [-10^6,10^6]. The polygon has positive area, no collinear successive edges and no self-intersections. Preserve input order. Return a boolean with exact boundary handling. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Scan all cyclic edge orientations toward P. Ignore zeros and reject if both a positive and a negative sign occur. Otherwise accept.
options.feedback: A convex polygon is the intersection of its inward closed half-planes. Either traversal direction makes all interior signs consistent, and zero allows exact boundary contact.

options.text: Compute the same n cyclic orientations into an array, then accept exactly if their nonzero signs do not mix.
options.feedback: It checks the correct half-planes but stores all values when two running sign flags suffice.

options.text: Return true when P lies in the polygon's inclusive coordinate bounding box.
options.feedback: The triangle [(0,0),(4,0),(0,4)] has bounding box [0,4] by [0,4], yet P=(3,3) is outside the triangle.

options.text: Accept only when every edge orientation toward P is strictly positive.
options.feedback: It rejects boundary points and also all interior points for clockwise input. Both are explicitly legal.

feedback.reason: Use consistent inward half-planes to test inclusive containment in a convex polygon.
details: Scan all cyclic edges, including last-to-first. Compute cross(next-current,P-current), remembering whether any positive and any negative value occurs. Return false as soon as both occur; otherwise return true. Zero values impose no sign.

A point in a convex polygon lies on the same orientation side of every directed edge, allowing zero for boundary points. Seeing both signs proves outside. This half-plane test relies on convexity and ordered polygon edges.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (consistent-edge-sides). Let n be the vertex count. Analyze the scan that returns early on mixed signs but otherwise visits all edges. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: An inside or boundary point forces n exact edge-orientation tests.
details: An inside or boundary query causes all n edge tests, so the scan has tight linear worst-case time. Each exact cross product costs constant work and has magnitude at most 8*10^12. Two sign flags and an index replace the orientation list. There is no input copy or preprocessing.
Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Correct: all edges can be visited with constant running sign state.
“O(log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A different specialized convex-polygon search could use logarithmic time, but the revealed method scans edges.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This describes retaining the orientation list, which the analyzed scan avoids.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The scan does not compare every pair of vertices.
